blocks.prompt: 9. A particle is projected vertically upwards with a velocity 100 m/s, and another is let fall from a height of 200 m at the same time. Find the height of the point where they meet each other.
blocks.explanation:
Two particles move on the same vertical line, both with acceleration \(g\) downward.
Given: one goes up from the ground at 100 m/s; the other falls from rest from 200 m. Find: the height where they meet.
Plan: write each height after \(t\) seconds, set them equal, solve for \(t\), then find the height (\(g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2\) as in the book).
steps:
Given: first particle \(u = 100\) m/s upward from the ground; second particle \(u = 0\) from a height of 200 m directly above it; both start at the same moment; \(g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2\).
To find: the height of the point where they meet.
Method: Measure heights upward from the ground. For each particle use \(x = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2\) (with \(a = -g\) for upward motion and \(a = g\) for downward motion, as in the book). They meet when both heights are equal.

Height of the first particle
\[h_1 = 100t + \dfrac{1}{2}(-9.8)t^2\]
\[h_1 = 100t - 4.9t^2 \quad (1)\]
Why: Upward is positive and gravity pulls downward, so \(a = -g\).

Height of the second particle
\[\text{fall} = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}(9.8)t^2 = 4.9t^2\]
\[h_2 = 200 - 4.9t^2 \quad (2)\]
Why: It starts from rest and falls with \(a = g\); its height is 200 m minus the distance it has fallen.

They meet when the heights are equal
\[100t - 4.9t^2 = 200 - 4.9t^2\]
\[100t = 200\]
\[t = 2\ \text{s}\]
Why: Meeting means being at the same place at the same time. The \(4.9t^2\) terms cancel because both particles have the same acceleration.

Height of the meeting point
\[h_1 = 100(2) - 4.9(2)^2\]
\[= 200 - 19.6 = 180.4\ \text{m}\]
Why: Put \(t = 2\) in (1).

Check
\[h_2 = 200 - 4.9(4) = 180.4\ \text{m}\ \checkmark\]
\[v_1 = 100 - 9.8(2) = 80.4\ \text{m/s}\]
Why: Equation (2) gives the same height. The first particle is still rising (\(v_1 > 0\)), so the meeting really happens on its way up, in the air.
blocks.final_answer: They meet \(180.4\) m above the ground, \(2\) s after the start.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: The book prints no answer for Exercise 7.1, so this answer is ours. It was checked independently with a computer algebra system and against an independent worked solution. We take, as the question intends, that the first particle is projected from the ground directly below the point from which the second is let fall. Shortcut: both have the same acceleration, so the 200 m gap closes at a steady 100 m/s, giving \(t = 2\) s at once.
